report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of drift.py: DriftReport.render, snapshot I/O functions, comparison helpers. Verified docstring claims against code.
risks: write_snapshot | medium | keep function uses prefix + v, but acceptance keys are stored with prefix (e.g., 'island:foo') while state values are bare (e.g., 'foo'); the prefix is prepended correctly, but if state values ever include the prefix, matching would double it. | Check that state values never include the prefix; or change keep to handle both forms.

_digest | low | docstring claims 'repo_state is INSIDE' but the code only includes it if present; if state lacks 'repo_state', doc.get returns None and digest still works. | Verify that state always contains 'repo_state' when digest is computed.
digest_ok | low | Returns True if doc.get(DIGEST_KEY) == _digest(doc); if doc[DIGEST_KEY] is missing, doc.get returns None and comparison fails as expected. | No action needed.
snapshot_bytes | low | Docstring says 'no timestamps' but does not enforce; code omits generated_at as described. | No action needed.
load_snapshot | low | Returns dict with '__error__' on parse failure; consumers must check for this key. | Ensure all callers handle '__error__'.
_remedy | low | Each branch returns a string; no fallback for unknown kind (would return None). | Add a default remedy or raise.
keep in write_snapshot | medium | The keep function filters state[key] using prefix + v; if prefix is empty, it would match all items. | Ensure prefix is never empty.

claims.text: A hash over the mechanical half only. ``acceptances`` is excluded because it is the one part a human is SUPPOSED to write; ``note`` because it is a constant.
claims.why: Lines 876-878: body = {k: doc.get(k) for k in _MECHANICAL_KEYS} excludes acceptances and note (note not in _MECHANICAL_KEYS).

claims.text: Canonical JSON with sorted keys, so the digest is a function of the values and not of the writer's key order -- two runs over an unchanged tree still produce identical bytes.
claims.why: Line 879: json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, ...) ensures sorted keys.

claims.text: ``repo_state`` is INSIDE, and that is not an accident. It is the field that says which tree was scanned, and a freshness stamp anybody can rewrite without invalidating the signature is decorative. The cost is that the digest changes on every commit even when no list moved -- which is correct: the snapshot really does describe a different tree.
claims.why: repo_state is in _MECHANICAL_KEYS (line 873), so it is included in body.

claims.text: Does this snapshot's own digest still cover its own mechanical lists?
claims.why: Line 888: return doc.get(DIGEST_KEY) == _digest(doc) checks if the stored digest matches a fresh digest of the mechanical keys.

claims.text: Public because it is not only :func:`check`'s business. Any verb that INHERITS lists from an existing snapshot rather than rescanning has to ask this first and refuse on a mismatch -- otherwise it re-signs whatever a text editor left behind and turns a caught hand-edit into a valid baseline.
claims.why: The claim about verbs that inherit lists is not verifiable in this chunk; no such verbs are defined here.

claims.text: The exact text of the snapshot. Sorted, no timestamps, trailing newline: two runs over an unchanged tree must produce byte-identical output or the git diff -- the thing a human actually reads -- becomes noise.
claims.why: Line 906: json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n" produces sorted (via earlier sorts) output with trailing newline; no timestamps in doc.

claims.text: ``repo_state`` comes out of ``state``, not out of a probe taken here, so this stays a pure function of its arguments. A clock reading would not: ``generated_at`` is absent from this artifact on purpose, because the question worth answering is "which tree" (``repo_state.head``, stable across a no-op regeneration) and not "at what o'clock" (different on every run, and therefore a diff on every run).
claims.why: Line 894: repo_state is taken from state.get('repo_state'); generated_at is not in the doc dict.

claims.text: Write the baseline, EXCLUDING every item that has an acceptance entry.
claims.why: Lines 920-931: accepted_keys = {a.item for a in acceptances}; keep function filters state[key] to exclude items whose prefixed key is in accepted_keys.

claims.text: This exclusion is the load-bearing part. If an accepted island were baked into ``islands``, ``--refresh`` would silently become a third, undated way to accept -- and being the easiest one, it would be the only one anybody used. Keeping accepted items out of the baseline means they stay live drift, suppressed only for as long as their date holds.
claims.why: The code explicitly removes accepted items from lists before writing (lines 924-931).

claims.text: not blocking: a test is evidence somebody intends to wire it. Wire it from a real entry point, or delete it -- this count is the one that grew to 55 the last time nobody watched it
claims.why: Line 966: return "not blocking: a test is evidence somebody intends to wire it. ..."

observations.what: The keep function in write_snapshot uses prefix + v to check against accepted_keys; if state values already contain the prefix, the concatenation would double it.
docstring for _digest claims repo_state is always included, but code uses doc.get('repo_state') which returns None if missing; digest still works.
digest_ok returns False if doc is not a dict or has __error__, but does not check if DIGEST_KEY exists; doc.get returns None, comparison fails.
snapshot_bytes docstring claims 'no timestamps' but does not enforce; code omits generated_at as described.
load_snapshot returns error dict with key __error__; consumers must check for this key to detect parse failures.
_remedy has no default return for unknown kind; would return None.
write_snapshot's keep function filters by prefix + v; if prefix is empty string, it would match all items.
